cover.headline: The FCA named *5* regulated activities AI agents can drift into.
cover.sub: A tech-provider label won't exempt you, it said on 24 Nov. Four changes from 23 to 25 Nov on who carries the duty, plus two courses.

items.title: The FCA: a tech label won't *exempt* your agent
items.statLabel: regulated activities the FCA lists for agent makers to check
items.what: 24 Nov: payments, financial promotions, an authorised information service, credit broking, advice. Being a tech provider doesn't remove the need for authorisation.
items.why: Firms are asked whether to accept payments an AI agent instructs. Map every action your agent can take to that list before you launch in the UK.

items.title: Claude's top models can log to *your* bucket
items.statLabel: calendar days your team gets to answer a Safety Case, per Anthropic's docs
items.what: 23 Nov: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in beta, and in preview on Bedrock. Prompts stay in your own cloud account. No AWS or Anthropic person reads them.
items.why: The misuse review moves to you. Lose access to the key or bucket and Bedrock stops serving these models in 24 hours. Name an owner first.

items.title: MCP servers can now ship *skills* to Claude
items.statLabel: monthly MCP SDK downloads, by Anthropic's count
items.what: 24 Nov, in beta: servers ship skills that update with the server. Tasks and Elicitation are GA for Pro, Max and Ultra, rolling out to Team and Enterprise.
items.why: The spec says to treat skill content as untrusted input. Pick the servers allowed to ship skills, and ask a person before any tool moves money.

items.title: 42 attorneys general fight an AI *chat auction*
items.statLabel: US accounts whose chats and personal data go to auction on 1 Dec
items.what: 24 Nov: they asked a court to reject Character.AI's sale. Its policy said it doesn't sell personal information. Under the terms, the buyer needn't honour that.
items.why: Every chat log and risk score you keep can be sold. Check what your privacy policy says happens to AI conversations in a sale or insolvency.

coursesTitle: How agents call *tools*, and how to scope them

courses.title: Stanford CS 329Z: Tool Use & Function Calling
courses.note: Lecture 4, given 5 Oct: why models need tools, interfaces from REST to MCP, and how to evaluate tool use. Its MCP reading is the 2025 spec.

courses.title: OAuth 2.0 Course for Beginners
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, 2 hours: an authorization server, a resource server and a client with PKCE. Posted 6 Jan, so not new.

read: The FCA keeps *authorisation* with whoever runs the agent. Anthropic and AWS moved *the misuse review* into your account. MCP put *skill vetting* on the host. 42 AGs say a *privacy promise* survives a sale.
takeaway: Name one owner per duty this week: the activity map, the Safety Case queue, the skills list, the privacy promise.
